title: Follow dependencies
intro: A chain runs dependent steps in order. Checking a draft requires that draft to exist, so these two steps cannot run independently.
takeaway: Use a chain when later work depends on an earlier result. Extra steps add latency and new failure points.

beats.text: First produce the draft. The check needs that output.
Send the draft to the checking step. The dependency is now available.
Check the draft against the criteria. Keep the observed findings.
Build the result from checked work. Order follows the data dependency.

title: Route to one specialist
intro: Routing selects a path based on the request. An API compatibility question goes to the reviewer equipped for that work.
takeaway: A route is a choice, not proof that the chosen worker will be correct. Ambiguous requests need a fallback.

beats.text: The request concerns API compatibility. Not every specialist needs to run.
A router chooses the relevant path. It uses the request and routing criteria.
Send the task to the API reviewer. Its tools and instructions fit that scope.
A new request has unclear scope. Send it to human triage instead.

title: Independent parallel work
intro: Two read-only reviews can inspect different concerns in the same code snapshot. Their analyses are independent, so they can overlap.
takeaway: Parallel work is appropriate when tasks do not depend on each other or mutate shared state unsafely.

beats.text: Freeze one code snapshot. Both reviewers must inspect that revision.
Assign compatibility and migration reviews. These analyses can run independently.
Both reviewers inspect the code. Neither edits shared files.
Keep the results tied to the snapshot. The coordinator will need both reports.

title: Join before deciding
intro: The final assessment depends on both reviews. One early result does not satisfy the join condition.
takeaway: A coordinator must handle missing, failed or conflicting results. Parallel execution does not remove dependencies at the decision point.

beats.text: In this run, the API review finishes first. The migration review is still running.
The coordinator waits for the dependency. One report cannot stand for both.
Migration finishes and reports a risk. Its report travels to the coordinator.
The migration risk blocks this release. Two reports do not imply success.

title: Revise against criteria
intro: An evaluator checks work against explicit criteria. Feedback can drive a revision loop, but the controller must limit iteration and handle uncertain grading.
takeaway: Evaluation is useful feedback, not infallible truth. Stop when criteria or budgets say to stop.

beats.text: The worker submits a draft. The evaluator applies explicit criteria.
The evaluator finds a missing requirement. Return a specific reason to revise.
The worker submits a revised result. The evaluator checks it again.
The revised example meets the criterion. Stop this loop after one revision.
